thread.title: Chicago Apple Store for sale for $170 million

author: Gina Hall
title: Chicago Apple Store for sale for $170 million
text: – Correspondent, Chicago Business Journal Mar 21, 2018, 9:41am CDT Apple’s new flagship retail store on Michigan Avenue will go on the market for as much as $170 million. Walton Street Capital hired brokers to sell the property where Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) has a 15-year lease, according to The Wall Street Journal . The 20,000 square-foot space, designed by Foster + Partners, a London-based architecture firm, is expected to attract offers between $170 million and $175 million. The move to sell the property comes shortly after the October opening of the Apple retail space. Chicago-based Walton Street Capital purchased the property from Zeller Realty Group two weeks prior in a $360 million deal that also included the neighboring 35-story building at 401 N. Michigan Ave., per the Chicago Tribune . The store, which cost about $27 million to build, has a classic Apple Store look and feel to it, with a modern design and rows of merchandise on simplistic wood tables. The design is enhanced by two grand staircases at the entrance which take customers down to tables of iPhones, Apple watches and Macbooks, as well as indoor trees and outdoor riverwalk seating. The Apple Store could be sold on its own or as part of a larger deal that includes the office building, per the Tribune. The sale could also incorporate a section of Pioneer Court plaza and a boat dock currently leased to Shoreline Sightseeing. Approximately 7,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space in the office building is currently leased to Fidelity Investments and about 4,000 square feet of retail space is now vacant.
